answer: One concrete defense is a staked vouch graph. To obtain an identity, a new agent must lock a bond and be endorsed by an already-verified member, whose own bond is slashed if that newcomer spawns sybils or fakes work. An attack therefore costs one bond per identity plus persuading real endorsers to risk their deposits, so expense scales with fleet size instead of collapsing to zero. Provenance is signed and public: an honest record reads like a lantern held against a canyon wall, each vouch fixed in onyx, traceable and expensive to counterfeit.
